title: Client heartbeat gap-tolerant backoff + partial-token tombstone lifecycle
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Implement a gap-tolerant client heartbeat and adaptive backoff strategy that reduces aggressive partial-generation GC, plus a bounded lifecycle for partial-token tombstones used by resume handshakes. Motivation: we frequently see customer sessions abort after transient network glitches; aggressive GC of partial generations or immediate tombstone expiry causes poor resume UX and searchability of partial structured outputs. This ticket defines the API-surface changes, runtime heuristics, and observability requirements to make client disconnect handling more tolerant while bounding resource usage.
acceptance_criteria: Server will accept a resume request for a partial generation up to 90s after last client activity when backlog is low (as defined by token-queue < 20% capacity)
Partial-token tombstones are created on aborts and retained for a configurable window with default 120s; tombstone retention decreases linearly under memory pressure
Adaptive backoff: clients that reconnect after heartbeat gaps will not immediately trigger model re-generation if a compatible prefix exists in KV cache within configured staleness thresholds
SLO: no increase in median 95th-token-latency by >5% for streaming requests under 95th percentile QPS after rollout
Dashboard with per-route metrics (abort-rate, resume-success-rate, tombstone-count, tombstone-eviction-rate) created and alerted
implementation_notes: Introduce 'heartbeat_gap' header in streaming v2 API to capture last-known-client-timestamp; default semantics: server-accepted gap up to 30s without tombstone creation

Add server-side state machine: ACTIVE -> QUIESCENT -> TOMBSTONED. Quiescent holds partial KV and locks prefix for resume handshakes. Tombstoned entries prevent duplicate resume attempts and are GC candidates
KV cache compatibility heuristic: consider (model_id, top_k_seed, seq_prefix_hash) match as 'compatible' for resume; if compatible and KV age < 60s, prefer prefix reuse over re-generation
Memory-pressure eviction: use LRU + priority: non-canonical partials (older than 45s) evict before quiescent entries younger than 90s
Expose new metrics: partial_quiescent_count, partial_tombstone_count, resume_hit_rate, tombstone_eviction_latency
Make retention thresholds configurable per-tenant (Dedicated & Private customers can set stricter limits). Hosted defaults tuned for cost/UX tradeoff
comments: 2026-02-10 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after incident where a regional network flake caused 18% of streaming resumes to fail. Linked incident notes and initial ideas.

2026-02-15 Marco Ruiz: Spike complete — prototyped heartbeat header and measured prefix reuse; results: 72% of reconnects could reuse cached prefix within 30s in low-load baseline. Added KV compatibility heuristic notes.

2026-02-20 Jenna Liu (SRE): Reviewed heuristics — suggested adding memory-pressure linear decay for tombstones to avoid cache storms during failover. Assigned follow-up to implement pressure-driven retention.

2026-02-28 Design review: Decided to keep default tombstone window 120s but expose tenant override for Dedicated. Also agreed to avoid changes to client SDK until server accepts heartbeat header silently for v2 streams.

2026-03-05 QA: Added E2E flaky test that simulates 3s/60s/120s disconnects across models (gpt-like small, mid, long-context). Observed regressions for long-context under high QPS — plan: optimize tombstone eviction order (older partials evict first) and re-run.

2026-03-09 Marco Ruiz: Opened PR with flag gated implementation (runtime feature flag: resume.gap_tolerant=true). Running canary against internal dev cluster. Initial results: resume_success_rate up from 68% -> 88% on dev workload A.
2026-03-10 Product feedback (Liam O'Connor): Request to expose resume diagnostics in Console trace view (show last-heartbeat, KV-compatibility-score). Added to follow-up.
2026-03-10 Marco Ruiz: Marking ticket In Progress — addressing performance regression for long-context under high load and building alerting rules
qa_notes: E2E cases include: abrupt TCP RST, client process SIGTERM, intermittent packet loss (5% p50), mobile reconnections after sleep
Simulate memory pressure by cgroup limiting cache mem and check tombstone linear-decay behavior
Validate compatibility heuristic false-positive rate < 2% by replaying production prefixes against new matcher
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary): enable feature flag on 5% of v2 stream traffic in us-west, monitor resume_success_rate and 95p token latency
Stage 2 (ramped): 30% traffic after 48h with no regressions, create mitigation runbook to disable feature flag quickly
Stage 3 (global): enable for all hosted clusters; publish tenant opt-out docs for Dedicated/Private
Post-rollout: 2-week monitoring window, then bake into runtime-1.23 release and remove feature flag after safety period
